projects.title: Enterprise AI Spend Approval Workflow
projects.description: Produced a prioritized review of an internal AI spending approval workflow and clearer guidance for applicants and approvers.
projects.summary: Internal AI purchases needed clearer approval criteria, rejection explanations, and resubmission paths. I reviewed the request lifecycle and turned recurring friction into a prioritized improvement report connecting applicant guidance, approver decisions, and cost ownership.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Analyzed sampled approval requests and grouped rejection patterns by spending tier, distinguishing personal subscriptions, organizational budgets, enterprise tools, APIs, and infrastructure.
Organized four improvement priorities: clearer rejection reasons, actionable approval and rejection wording, organization-leader notifications, and confusing form elements.
Recommended tier-specific inputs rather than a uniform form, so the required evidence matched the scale and purpose of each request.
Proposed a lifecycle record linking tool owner, business purpose, data risk, approval, recurring cost, expected benefit, and next review date.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered an improvement report, applicant guidance, and approver notification wording for the AI operations team.
Selected changes reached development: tier-specific inputs, rejection-reason and confirmation fields, usage visibility in the collaboration app, and clearer guidance messages.

projects.status: Improvement report delivered and selected changes implemented in development. The broader lifecycle record remains a proposal.

projects.title: AI Approval Workflow Impact Review
projects.description: Built a matched-window review of an approval workflow release and a dashboard of request themes.
projects.summary: A release changed the AI spending approval form and its guidance. I assessed what changed in request behavior and whether previously identified issues were addressed, using comparable observation windows rather than unequal before-and-after periods.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Analyzed 800+ requests around the rollout and identified the release boundary from the appearance of new fields.
Recalculated the comparison with matched windows and assessed guidance issues separately from request-volume and approval metrics.
Built organization-by-reason heatmaps with switches for request count, average and total amount, approval rate, and self-approval rate.
Separated incomplete classifier coverage from genuinely ambiguous requests, and reviewed turnaround by time band.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered standalone HTML reports for the release comparison and request patterns, with findings prepared for the AI operations team.
Made classification gaps and unresolved guidance issues visible without publishing internal approval rates or spending amounts.

projects.status: Analysis and reports completed. Before-and-after associations do not establish the release as the sole cause.

projects.title: Enterprise AI Adoption Survey
projects.description: Designed and ran a multilingual enterprise survey measuring AI use across tasks and cross-team workflows.
projects.summary: The company needed a consistent picture of AI adoption across headquarters and subsidiaries. I designed a multilingual survey that separated individual work from cross-team workflows, making automation maturity and employee needs comparable across organizational groups.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Structured the questionnaire around respondents’ main tasks and shared workflows, using a six-stage automation scale.
Prepared Korean, English, and Japanese versions and coordinated distribution and participation reminders across business units.
Reconciled approximately 1k responses with the matched participant records used for analysis, keeping collection and processing stages distinct.
Designed the response structure to support comparisons by job family, organization, task complexity, and workflow automation.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered the survey instrument, multilingual communications, and a reconciled response dataset for downstream analysis.
Established a shared measurement structure for the automation dashboard and executive reporting workstreams.

projects.status: Survey delivered and approximately 1k response records prepared for analysis; counts are rounded.

projects.title: Task & Workflow Automation Analysis
projects.description: Turned multilingual survey responses into comparable automation measures and an analysis dashboard.
projects.summary: Survey responses contained multilingual descriptions of tasks and workflows that could not be compared reliably without preprocessing. I converted them into structured automation measures and dashboards that preserved the difference between task-level and workflow-level analysis.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Processed and reconciled raw responses in Python, translating free text before job-family and work-type classification.
Analyzed 2k+ automation cases, comparing task steps, workflow complexity, and adoption patterns across headquarters and subsidiaries.
Reduced unclassified responses through translation and category refinement, then compared patterns across technical, design, and other job families.
Mapped questionnaire items to automation measures and documented where different denominators prevented direct comparison.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Built an automation-analysis dashboard with organizational, job-family, task, and workflow views.
Produced a survey retrospective explaining how difficulty describing work affected measurement and future survey design.

projects.status: Analysis and dashboards completed. Case counts are rounded; task and workflow measures use distinct units.

projects.title: AI Transformation Executive Report
projects.description: Prepared an executive report connecting AI adoption findings to priorities for governance and implementation.
projects.summary: Leadership needed an actionable interpretation of the adoption survey beyond participation figures. I connected organization-level findings, workflow bottlenecks, and employee requests to a phased plan for deeper AI use and practical governance.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Created a 20–30-slide executive report covering broad adoption, depth of automation, organizational differences, and an integrated dashboard.
Separated management priorities—cost, policy, time, and sponsorship—from execution priorities such as technology, training, examples, and collaboration.
Mapped questions to adoption dimensions and developed a proxy measure for the gap between expected and actual automation.
Removed duplicated questions and organized section-level findings around decisions for corporate functions and production studios.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Prepared the executive summary, responsive dashboard, and phased action plan for a CEO briefing.
Translated survey evidence into priorities for the AI transformation team while keeping proposed automation targets distinct from measured results.

projects.status: Executive materials prepared for leadership review; report size is presented as a range.

projects.title: Q2 AI Cost Trend Report
projects.description: Automated quarterly AI cost reporting and identified subscription and API optimization opportunities.
projects.summary: Monthly AI administration files did not provide a single view of organizational spending or subscription economics. I built a consolidated report to explain cost changes, surface attribution gaps, and assess which users might benefit from a different plan.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Built a Python generator that converted monthly administration workbooks into one navigable HTML report for senior leadership.
Used quarterly totals and explicit small-base categories to prevent negligible spending from appearing as misleading percentage growth.
Classified purpose-labeled keys into development, agents, review, translation, documentation, and bots, while surfacing keys with missing purpose metadata.
Cross-checked high-spend accounts against subscription tiers and compared observed costs before and after migration.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered an executive cost report with organization-level change views, model adoption patterns, and user-level plan comparisons.
Identified a remaining migration opportunity and an adoption gap; monetary amounts and internal account counts remain anonymized.

projects.status: Report and account comparisons completed; future migration savings remain estimates.

projects.title: Model Migration: Cost vs. Usage
projects.description: Evaluated a model migration across API and enterprise channels without assuming lower unit prices meant lower total spend.
projects.summary: A model migration reduced unit prices, but that alone did not establish a reduction in total spending. I compared pricing, token volume, and billed costs across API and enterprise channels to assess the actual economics of the transition.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Produced an executive before-and-after report with separate API and enterprise-channel views and adoption patterns by account group.
Found that increased usage absorbed the price improvement during the reviewed period, so the analysis did not confirm a net saving.
Checked price changes outside the targeted migration to avoid attributing all vendor price reductions to the announcement.
Flagged missing historical data when one channel’s apparent effective prices increased by roughly an order of magnitude, and excluded unreliable cost-change findings.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered standalone HTML cost dashboards and a model-selection guide with the underlying data retained.
Clarified the decision between encouraging productive use and controlling aggregate spending, with data-quality limitations visible in the report.

projects.status: Executive analysis completed; no net saving was confirmed in the observed period.

projects.title: AI Budget Validation & Forecast
projects.description: Built a reconciled AI cost outlook with scenarios that separated existing commitments from new funding decisions.
projects.summary: The budget decision required separating existing contractual commitments from new spending capacity. I reconciled actuals, billing periods, annual seats, usage-based costs, and vendor credits before building forward scenarios for leadership.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Combined year-to-date spending with three run-rate scenarios: lower, baseline, and higher usage growth.
Corrected a billing-versus-usage-month mismatch and separated annual personal subscriptions and seat commitments from monthly usage costs.
Compared full, partial, and limited cloud-platform migration scenarios, keeping credits separate from recurring costs and their effective dates.
Validated the Finance submission under a consistent exchange-rate assumption and documented a material input discrepancy before executive reporting.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered a standalone HTML outlook for the remaining months of the year, with scenario comparisons and reconciliation notes.
Clarified the incremental funding decision and prevented committed costs from being counted again; budgets, vendor credits, and internal forecasts are anonymized.

projects.status: Forecast and financial reconciliation delivered; scenarios represent projections.

projects.title: AI Spend Categories & Optimization Priorities
projects.description: Produced a cross-product AI spending analysis and ranked practical optimization opportunities.
projects.summary: AI spending was fragmented across users, models, subscriptions, and organizational records. I combined these sources to show where usage was concentrated and which optimization opportunities deserved review first.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Joined user-level monthly ledgers, product and model records, and HR data into a reviewable analysis dataset.
Compared API and subscription spending, premium-model concentration, low-use enterprise seats, and overlapping coding tools.
Identified four review priorities and distinguished directly observed usage from provisional estimates of agent and coding activity.
Documented overlapping category populations and missing product surfaces so cost totals were not combined incorrectly.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered a standalone HTML report and joined workbook for management and executive reporting.
Prioritized model review, seat utilization, subscription overlap, and vendor consolidation without exposing internal spend or user counts.

projects.status: Analysis and optimization priorities delivered; inferred usage categories remain labeled.

projects.title: Model Transition & Tiering Plan
projects.description: Developed a staged transition plan from legacy premium models to a smaller cost-tiered model catalog.
projects.summary: Legacy premium models represented a material share of spending while successor models offered a different price-performance trade-off. I developed a staged transition proposal that preserved an exception path and required measurement after migration.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Reviewed monthly model usage across API and enterprise channels and repriced the same token volume under successor-model rates.
Grouped models into low-, medium-, and high-cost tiers, proposing one or two standard options per tier.
Designed three rollout stages: stop new legacy use, phase down existing premium use with approved exceptions, and track realized costs.
Separated vendor-announced performance claims from the limited internal observations available for the successor model.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Produced an HTML migration plan with tiering, affected-population analysis, exception handling, and post-transition measurement.
Presented potential savings as a constant-volume scenario; confidential financial amounts and account counts were omitted.

projects.status: Transition plan prepared; projected savings depend on adoption and actual usage.

projects.title: Agent Leaderboard & Registry Hygiene
projects.description: Analyzed agent activity to identify attribution gaps and registry quality issues.
projects.summary: An agent activity leaderboard could support governance only if identities, usage, and credits were attributed consistently. I reviewed activity concentration and registry quality before interpreting the efficiency of individual agents.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Analyzed 80+ agents over approximately three months, comparing recorded tokens, credits, and concentration of activity.
Identified substantial token use without corresponding credits as a possible attribution gap requiring registry review.
Flagged duplicate names and test or personal agents that could distort rankings and cost ownership.
Compared credit efficiency while keeping the unconfirmed monetary value of a credit outside the analysis.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered an activity report with attribution gaps, registry-cleanup priorities, and efficiency differences.
Provided evidence for agent identity and cost-governance work without treating incomplete rankings as validated financial performance.

projects.status: Activity and registry analysis completed; scope figures are rounded.

projects.title: ChatGPT & Codex Overage Validation
projects.description: Reconciled an AI service overage invoice and documented the billing treatment.
projects.summary: An enterprise AI overage needed to be reconciled against a one-time vendor waiver and subsequent billing obligations. I checked the affected period and invoice treatment so future settlement was not confused with the exceptional credit.

sections.title: Approach and contribution

Documented the boundary between the one-time waiver and the resumption of normal overage settlement.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope

The outcome records invoice validation; it does not assign the vendor’s waiver to a personal negotiation.

projects.status: Invoice status and settlement boundary confirmed.

projects.title: AI Model Matrix & Playground

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Deployed the comparison playground and produced methodology, unit-price, and value-line reports.

projects.title: Task-to-Model Matching & AA Integration

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Produced a selection-table design, integration notes, and a benchmark-access review document.

projects.title: MVI & Human-Equivalent Hours
projects.description: Produced model-value and human-work-equivalent measurement concepts with explicit comparability limits.
projects.summary: Price-only comparisons miss the time and quality of the work a model performs. I explored a model-value framework combining task performance, unit price, and human-equivalent effort, then identified limits in the proposed calculations.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Designed an approach to calibrate AI task time against Human-Equivalent Hours.
Defined a task-specific Model Value Index and developed a dashboard mockup and project report.
Identified that performance scores could not be compared indiscriminately across different tasks.
Documented conflicts between estimated blended prices and the intended governance objective, deferring a combined score until the method was defensible.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Produced measurement definitions, calibration concepts, and visual mockups for cost-versus-value discussions.
Preserved the framework as research and design work rather than presenting an exploratory score as a production standard.

projects.status: Framework and mockups completed; combined scoring remains under methodological review.

projects.title: API & Agent Cost Optimization Strategy
projects.description: Wrote an API and agent cost strategy organized around diagnosis, technical levers, and ongoing governance.
projects.summary: API cost optimization involved architecture and workflow design as well as model prices. I organized a strategy around diagnosis, targeted improvements, and governance so teams could select the right intervention for their cost pattern.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Structured the plan around three phases: diagnose usage, improve the relevant cost levers, and formalize governance.
Defined three lever groups: prompt and context, model selection and execution mode, and agent loops and design.
Reviewed native cloud prompt-cache support and proposed checking adoption across deployment projects before adding separate infrastructure.
Used observed subscription-migration work as a precedent for measuring outcomes rather than relying solely on vendor claims.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered a strategy document covering caching, context management, routing, batching, and agent-loop controls.
Proposed a scoped pilot and measurement sequence for the AI engineering and governance teams.

projects.status: Optimization strategy delivered; the pilot remained proposed.

projects.title: Cost Taxonomy & Measurement Rollout
projects.description: Designed a cost attribution taxonomy and rollout plan for AI API usage.
projects.summary: Aggregate API bills did not explain which team, workflow, or environment generated the cost. I designed a cost-attribution taxonomy and a staged measurement plan that could begin before a central gateway was fully available.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Defined four attribution dimensions: team, use case, environment, and usage pattern.
Separated measurement, adoption, and enforcement so log-based diagnosis could start before gateway policy controls were complete.
Prepared least-privilege requests for log configuration and viewing, inference-profile tagging, and cost-report access.
Built a status board distinguishing completed work, current work, next actions, and infrastructure blockers.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Produced the attribution taxonomy, phased rollout plan, access requirements, and workstream status board.
Connected organizational ownership to usage evidence while keeping required cloud administration permissions explicit.

projects.status: Measurement plan and taxonomy prepared; infrastructure access remained a dependency.

projects.title: Context Compression Tool Evaluation
projects.description: Evaluated context compression options against native API and agent efficiency controls.
projects.summary: Third-party context-compression tools promised lower coding-agent costs, but their value depended on the actual workload. I compared those options with native optimization levers to recommend a practical pilot sequence.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Reviewed two compression tools and compared them with caching, model routing, context management, batching, and hard loop limits.
Recommended prioritizing native levers before introducing additional tool dependencies.
Made a compression-tool pilot conditional on evidence that the relevant coding-agent cost category was sufficiently large.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered a comparative evaluation and a staged pilot recommendation.
Defined the workload condition for a useful pilot rather than reporting unmeasured production savings.

projects.status: Tool evaluation completed; pilot and savings validation remained prospective.

projects.title: Enterprise Prompt Caching Strategy

projects.summary: Prompt caching required a consistent rollout approach across workflows rather than isolated configuration changes. I documented how to measure adoption, expand use, and introduce enforcement alongside broader API cost governance.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Defined three operating layers: measurement, adoption, and enforcement.
Linked the caching strategy to a phased API optimization plan so teams could establish evidence before enforcing controls.
Coordinated the documentation with API-key management and agent-cost governance to connect technical use with ownership.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered a prompt-caching strategy and supporting control documents.
Created a common direction for workflow adoption and future monitoring; infrastructure implementation remained a separate workstream.

projects.title: API Key Management Framework

Considered review, adoption, and sunset decisions as part of access management rather than treating key issuance as the final step.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Produced an API-key management framework and infrastructure direction alongside caching and agent-cost documentation.
Outlined an access lifecycle for AI engineers and governance owners; the full feature set was not confirmed as implemented.

projects.status: Framework and MVP scope documented; full enforcement remained unconfirmed.

projects.title: Agent Cost Governance & Monitoring
projects.description: Prepared an agent cost governance report focused on task-level measurement and runaway-execution safeguards.
projects.summary: Agent costs can grow through repeated steps, retries, and loops even when individual calls look inexpensive. I extended the governance approach from aggregate token spending to task-level monitoring and safeguards.

sections.title: Approach and contribution
paragraphs: Specified monitoring for cost per task, step count, retry rate, and cost-threshold alerts.
Connected these measures to a shared agent-cost report, API-key framework, and caching strategy.
Identified hard loop limits, compressed tool results, and separate planning and execution models as optimization practices for review.
Kept planned monitoring and alert work distinct from a continuously operated production system.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered an agent-cost governance report and monitoring roadmap for the AI engineering team.
Defined the task-level evidence needed to diagnose expensive runs and prioritize future controls.

projects.status: Governance report and monitoring roadmap completed; alert rollout remained planned.

Designed the approval pipeline in an enterprise workflow platform.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered a cost-classification design and approval-pipeline structure.
Connected intake, cost ownership, and lifecycle review within the broader AI governance operating model.

projects.title: AI Tool Intake & Risk Classification

sections.title: Approach and contribution

Consolidated review requirements into an initial guide and framed focused questions for Legal and Security.
Built the intake and approval flow in an enterprise workflow platform.

sections.title: Deliverables and scope
paragraphs: Delivered the adoption guide, evaluation criteria, and operational intake pipeline.
Provided a repeatable path from tool request to risk classification and approval.

projects.title: AI Safety Committee Workstream
